rounds.learn: A list comprehension builds a new list in one line. Read [n * 2 for n in nums] like this: n times 2, for each n in nums.
rounds.task: Double every number in a list.
rounds.code:
nums = [1, 2, 3]
doubled = [n * 2 for n in nums]
print(doubled)
rounds.say: [2, 4, 6]. A whole loop in one line.

rounds.learn: Add an if at the end to keep only some items. [n for n in nums if n > 2] keeps the numbers bigger than 2.
rounds.code:
nums = [1, 5, 2, 8]
big = [n for n in nums [[if]] n > 2]
[[print]](big)

rounds.task: Make every word in words loud, in one line.
Use a list comprehension to make the squares of 1, 2, 3 and 4. Print the list.
rounds.hint: print([n * n for n in range(1, 5)])
rounds.solution:
squares = [n * n for n in range(1, 5)]
print(squares)

checks.msg: Build it with [ ... for ... ] in one line.

rounds.say: %out%. That is the fancy one, done from memory.
